title: Modelling neural coding in the auditory midbrain with high resolution and accuracy
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Predict inferior-colliculus multi-unit spike-count activity for the original Fig. 4b,d seven-animal/four-sound evaluation. Preserve both trial-specific neural response prediction and reliability-normalized assessment; this scope does not include whole-paper new-animal adaptation or ASR.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Predict inferior-colliculus multi-unit spike-count activity for the original Fig. 4b,d seven-animal/four-sound evaluation. Preserve both trial-specific neural response prediction and reliability-normalized assessment; this scope does not include whole-paper new-animal adaptation or ASR.

Source-paper comparison for Fraction of explainable correlation explained (%) on each of the four original Fig. 4b sounds: Primary explained correlation (%) = 50*[rho(vec(R1),vec(Rhat1)) + rho(vec(R2),vec(Rhat2))]/rho(vec(R1),vec(R2)), equation (3). Rhat is sampled model activity; the separate variance metric uses predicted expected counts and source equations (4)-(5). Raw RMSE or ordinary correlation is not interchangeable.
success_criteria: Reproduce the source ICNet result using the exact original seven animals, both successive trials, four sounds, reliability masks, measurement times, alignment and equation (3) aggregation.

Freeze and evaluate a candidate against the published per-sound vector and a verified author baseline, with justified meaningful effect and animal-aware uncertainty over every sound; retain variance and unit-level results as source-comparable checks.

Resolve lawful access to the original development/training recordings and a matched access/resource policy; do not tune using the public four-sound evaluation responses and then call the score source-equivalent generalization.
The legacy four-fold held-sound program, trial1 calibration/trial2 scoring, response subset or different animal panel may support labeled extensions only, never a same-task paper win.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
